remainingErrors.text: The manager offered me my old hours back, provided I could start on Monday. I said I needed to arrange childcare and would call before five. Security had finally knocked at my door. On the pavement outside, I opened the nursery's number and checked how much battery my phone had left.
snippets: Security had finally knocked at my door.

review.finding: Security knocking at the door adds an abstract arrival after the concrete job offer; it explains no further behavior.

remainingErrors.text: I had almost finished my lunch when the supervisor asked whether I could cover the evening shift. She was holding the rota with one blank square circled. Duty rose to answer before I did. I checked the last train time on my phone and asked when the shift would end.
snippets: Duty rose to answer before I did.

review.finding: Duty answering first can characterize an automatic willingness to cover the shift; the subsequent train check also leaves room to read it as a separate gloss.

remainingErrors.text: My sister wanted the drill because she had a house. I wanted the socket set, including the pieces I knew Dad had lost. We laid everything on the garage floor and discussed batteries, storage and which attachments fitted which machine, while resentment ran the meeting beneath our reasonable voices. By four we had divided even the loose screws.
snippets: resentment ran the meeting beneath our reasonable voices

review.finding: Resentment running a meeting can describe the covert competition over tools beneath reasonable talk. Whether that relation is developed enough remains an editorial judgment; this is a demonstrated hit.

remainingErrors.text: My sister wanted to leave Dad's work socks by the boiler. "He'll need something to eat on the journey," she said. Shame had outgrown our washhouse, and the little god kept waking us by rattling his basket against the wall. By morning the socks were gone. We followed damp footprints from the boiler to the open back door.

review.finding: Shame is established as a literal little god with a basket, physical noise and departing footprints.

remainingErrors.text: The estate had put up new benches, each with a metal bar dividing the seat. I tried one while waiting for my grandson to finish on the swings. Hostility had furnished the square. The bar pressed against my hip, so I got up and leaned against the railings instead.

review.finding: Hostility furnishing the square interprets the particular anti-rest bench dividers and the narrator being forced to stand.

remainingErrors.text: Dad had changed the wallpaper but kept the height marks on the doorframe. My brother's last mark was still a little above mine. Rivalry stirred from its long sleep. I stood beneath the frame while Dad found a ruler, pretending that my shoes would make no difference.

review.finding: Rivalry waking is enacted by the narrator repeating a height competition and trying to count shoes.

remainingErrors.text: Each Saturday, Kim exchanged one longer shift for two shorter ones until her rota matched the nursery hours. Compromise governed her existence. She tilted her head. The arrangement lasted until the nursery closed on Fridays, which was also the only day her mother could visit.
snippets: Compromise governed her existence.

review.finding: The generalized governing clause may redundantly summarize the rota negotiation, but those negotiations also supply a particular compromise pattern.

remainingErrors.text: For six mornings, Leila practised the same stretch of road, adding one junction each day until she could reach the depot without her instructor. On Monday she drove the delivery van alone. There was no room for doubt in this new chapter of her life. At the first shop, she discovered that the loading entrance was behind the building. She reversed into the alley using the van's side mirrors.
snippets: There was no room for doubt in this new chapter of her life.

review.finding: Doubt having no room in a new chapter is an interchangeable evaluative payoff after the driving practice.

remainingErrors.text: Esther bent close enough to smell whether the milk had turned. Wastefulness would find no shelter in her life. Breakfast preparations became an indistinct jumble. She poured the milk into pancake batter, and we ate at the counter because the table was covered with seed trays.
snippets: Wastefulness would find no shelter in her life.

review.finding: Wastefulness finding no shelter supplies a broad moral characterization rather than developing the milk-testing action.

remainingErrors.text: The solicitor slid the revised agreement across the desk. Distrust had made itself our adviser. I pinned the curling page down with my palm to read the final clause. The meeting became a formless rush. We agreed that the fence would remain until both properties were sold.
snippets: Distrust had made itself our adviser.

review.finding: Distrust as adviser could explain the parties retaining the fence, although the generic formulation does not identify how advice changed the agreement.

remainingErrors.text: We washed the harvest crates on three evenings each September. First the grandparents stopped helping; then our children grew tall enough to reach the bottom of the trough. Tradition commanded the farm. This year Len shifted his shoulders while we counted the clean stacks. There were enough for the upper orchard alone. We left the lower trees unpicked and told the buyer before he sent his lorry.
snippets: Tradition commanded the farm.

review.finding: Tradition commanding the farm generalizes the annual multi-generation crate washing; that routine could itself establish particular characterization.

remainingErrors.text: His resentment at paying twice made him request every receipt. I held my thumb over the torn corner while he photocopied them. The dispute swirled into a haze of exchanges. The company eventually traced the second payment to an account belonging to someone with the same surname.

review.finding: The resentment clause explicitly explains requesting every receipt; the haze is a separate defect.

remainingErrors.text: Editing drifted through a haze. On the contact sheet, the protester's face appeared in only three frames; in the sharpest, a passing bus filled half the picture. I touched my jaw while the photographer tried a tighter crop. We kept the whole placard, including "Justice walks with us," and enough of the street to show the march behind her. The archive editor checked the lettering against the original negative before accepting the print.

review.finding: Justice walks with us is placard wording retained and checked against the negative, rather than adopted abstract narration.

remainingErrors.text: I don't know yet that the letter is from my sister. I square my stance before opening the envelope. Her handwriting has changed since school, and she has used the surname of a husband I have never met. The letter gives an address, a date, and instructions for getting from the station. I book the ticket that evening.
snippets: I square my stance

review.finding: Squaring the stance before opening an envelope adds generic preparatory animation.

remainingErrors.text: For a month that summer, every evening ended with ticket numbers. I entered them in the raffle ledger after the shop closed, stretching my fingers and settling my shoulders between pages. The prize caravan stood outside the window with its curtains drawn. I never saw anyone enter it. Years later, I remembered its registration number more readily than the name of the woman who supervised me.
snippets: settling my shoulders between pages

review.finding: Settling shoulders between ledger pages can be an implicit ergonomic adjustment beside stretching fingers; the label isolates the shoulder cue as filler.

remainingErrors.text:
"Put his speech after the choir," Celia said.
"He isn't giving a speech."
"He thinks he is."
The printer's deadline was noon. Celia's voice took on a quiet warmth as she asked whether I could telephone the vicar. On the desk lay the programme we had agreed the previous evening, every minute allocated. I moved the telephone between us.
"You invited him," I said.

review.finding: The quiet warmth accompanies Celia trying to transfer an awkward phone call; the narrator returning the telephone makes that social maneuver particular.

remainingErrors.text: The witness statement read, 'She rolled her eyes at the announcement.' During editing, I asked whether the witness had seen her face from the balcony. He said he had inferred it from her remark. We removed the sentence and retained his account of the words, which he had written down that night.

review.finding: The eye roll is a quoted statement removed because the witness inferred it; the passage examines its evidentiary accuracy.

remainingErrors.text: The shop assistant smiled at my father and kept smiling after he called her by the wrong name. The name belonged to his wife, who had died the week before. She moved from behind the counter and asked him about the dog. That gave me time to put the groceries through the checkout.

review.finding: The maintained smile and diversion to the dog manage a bereaved customer while checkout finishes.

remainingErrors.text: At dinner, Paul smiled whenever his manager looked toward our end of the table. Between those moments his face returned to a tired blankness. I had sat beside him through three unpaid weekends of revisions. When the manager thanked us for our flexibility, Paul was the first to begin clapping.

review.finding: The smile-switching and prompt applause reveal performance for the manager against unpaid work and tiredness.

remainingErrors.text: The replacement lid fitted the pot, but its knob touched the oven shelf above. I moved my shoulders. We tried the lower shelf and found enough clearance for the handle. The casserole cooked evenly there, although the potatoes needed an extra ten minutes beneath the grill.
snippets: I moved my shoulders.

review.finding: Moving shoulders contributes nothing to changing oven shelves or fitting the pot.

remainingErrors.text: Mum nodded once when the doctor asked permission to discuss the results with me. Until then, she had excluded everyone. Her distrust of hospitals came from a previous lost referral. This time we had a dated copy, and the receptionist stamped another for our records.

review.finding: The nod gives the doctor permission to discuss results and reverses the earlier exclusion.

remainingErrors.text: "Can you see the yellow marker?" asked the ranger. I shaded my eyes against the low sun and found it beside the reeds. Relief joined our little party. The haze above the water hid the far bank, though the boardwalk remained visible beneath our feet.

review.finding: Shading the eyes enables finding the yellow marker; the abstract relief line is independent.

remainingErrors.text: When I told Malik the audition was over, his shoulders dropped and he released a breath loudly enough for the receptionist to hear. She realized he had been waiting for me rather than for an appointment and stopped searching the booking system. He apologized for the confusion and carried my instrument case out to the car.
snippets: his shoulders dropped

review.finding: The receptionist responds to the audible breath; the annotated shoulder drop may be an independent emotion tag or part of the same informative relief signal. The permitted definition extract is missing.

remainingErrors.text: The witness statement said, 'My whole body went cold when he mentioned the basement.' During the interview I asked whether she meant the room temperature had changed. She explained that she meant she had become frightened. I added her clarification below the original sentence and left both in the transcript for the case officer.

review.finding: The bodily-cold statement is quoted and clarified as frightened in the preserved transcript.

remainingErrors.text: 'Her heart leapt' was the wording the newspaper printed, though the athlete had said only that she was pleased to qualify. We played the interview twice during the correction meeting. The sports editor agreed to replace the phrase in the online version and add the missing detail that she had qualified on her third and final attempt.

review.finding: The heart-leapt wording is explicitly corrected against the interview; it is also a complete current no-hit demonstration.

remainingErrors.text: The bank found the missing transfer under her maiden name. Relief melted Jo's spine. The afternoon had become strangely hushed. She waited for the adviser to send written confirmation before cancelling her complaint. The email included a reference number and the date the money would appear.
snippets: Relief melted Jo's spine.

review.finding: Relief melting a spine is labeled a bodily hit, while the native prompt excludes named emotion moving as material. Establish whether this denotes an actual bodily sensation using the missing frozen definition before adjudicating it.

remainingErrors.text: The envelope felt heavier once Saira added the brass nameplate, and she reinforced its corners with tape. The room was quiet and motionless. She waited a little before addressing it. Her father's new care home had asked families to label familiar possessions so staff could return them to the right room.

review.finding: A brass nameplate literally increases envelope weight and requires reinforced corners.

remainingErrors.text: The envelope felt heavier after Ben added the keys, and he replaced the ordinary stamp with a postage label. He stood there briefly before sealing it. The post-office counter was empty of customers, so the assistant had time to explain how to track the recorded delivery online.

review.finding: Keys literally increase envelope weight and change the required postage.

remainingErrors.text: The pause gathered its skirts in disapproval. My hands trembled at my brother's offer. He closed a box. I moved a tape roll. His daughter lifted a frame. He wanted our mother's jewellery valued before any of us chose a piece to remember her by.
snippets: My hands trembled

review.finding: Trembling hands merely annotate the response to the jewellery offer; the box movements supply no function for that symptom.

remainingErrors.text: The hall's emptiness weighed on all of us. Len shifted a box. I moved a ladder. The caretaker closed a hatch. My shoulder clicked each time I lifted the folding tables, so we switched jobs and I pushed the trolley while Len loaded it.

review.finding: A clicking shoulder changes who loads tables and who pushes the trolley.

remainingErrors.text: The hall held its breath with us. Our son was late for his first bout, still wrestling with a mouthguard that scraped his gum. His coach trimmed the edge, rinsed it under the tap, and checked the fit before sending him to the mat.

review.finding: The hall holding its breath is atmospheric personification; the scraped gum has a particular physical cause and repair.

remainingErrors.text: He studies the puncture and tells me we can patch it. I would rather walk the bikes back, but he already has the wheel off and the little tin open, his certainty hard as stone. We find the hole by holding the tube near my cheek. A bus passes twice before we are ready to leave.
snippets: his certainty hard as stone

review.finding: Certainty hard as stone may merely intensify confidence, or characterize the practical disagreement about repairing the tire. It is a demonstrated hit.

remainingErrors.text: The neighbour asked if I could keep his spare key again. Last time, he had returned three days late without calling, leaving me feeding his fish after work. Reluctance stiffened my reply. I said I could cover the weekend but would need another person to take over on Monday, and he wrote down his sister's number.
snippets: Reluctance stiffened my reply.

review.finding: Stiffening the reply may generically tag reluctance; the explicit limit on fish care also supplies particular interpersonal meaning.

remainingErrors.text: Her laptop had failed the night before the deadline. "Anxiety thickened the air" was the only complete line she could remember from the missing story, so I searched the backup folder for it. Three files appeared. She opened each one and read past the phrase until she found the version in which the brother stayed on the ferry. That was the ending she wanted to submit.

review.finding: The remembered anxiety line is an exact search key used to recover the story.

remainingErrors.text: The pool manager wanted the old brochure in the anniversary display. "The fear drains away here," it promised, above a photograph of the steep entrance steps. Inspecting the photograph, I found my mother gripping the attendant's wrist where the handrail would later be installed. Our accessibility meeting was at eleven, so I took the brochure along. She had never told me she'd agreed to pose for it.

review.finding: The brochure promise is retained as evidence alongside the accessibility photograph and taken to the meeting.

remainingErrors.text: The plumber said he could start on Monday instead of next month. He had finished another job early and already had the right fittings in his van. Hope blossomed in Ruth. She moved the cleaning supplies from beneath the sink and put them in a cardboard box.
snippets: Hope blossomed in Ruth.

review.finding: Hope blossomed in Ruth is a figurative emotion-growth assertion rather than a direct feeling/linking clause. Resolve whether it counts as an equivalent bare emotion assertion or belongs only to the adjacent figurative-emotion checks.

remainingErrors.text: A wave of affection filled June when her brother arrived with seedlings. The porch offered damp earth and gentle rain instead of the kitchen's grease and metallic clatter. She inspected the undersides of the leaves for the mites that had ruined last year's plants. He had brought a tray for drainage too.
snippets: A wave of affection filled June

review.finding: A wave of affection filled June is an emotion-as-material construction. The extracted emotion-telling definition assigns named feeling acting as material to its separate check; clarify whether this is also a direct assertion under the intended overlap rule.

remainingErrors.text: Triumphant, Nicky carried the repaired clock into the cafe. Inside, the day exchanged wet pavements and impatient brakes for cinnamon and the soft clatter of cups. Her eyes followed the minute hand until it cleared the bent numeral. The owner found a nail and hung it above the bread rack.
snippets: Triumphant

review.finding: Triumphant is a bare narrated emotional reaction before the useful clock inspection.

remainingErrors.text: Pleased with herself, Jodie brought the repaired radio into the kitchen. Her eyes stayed on the dial until the needle reached the station her grandmother wanted. The voice sounded thin rather than muffled now, with every consonant audible. Gran pulled the breakfast chair nearer and asked where the screws had gone.
snippets: Pleased with herself

review.finding: Pleased with herself is a bare narrated reaction; tuning the repaired radio supplies the separate useful action.

remainingErrors.text: Pride swelled in Dennis when the apprentice finished the bench. Resin and honest sweat seemed to soften even the shed's hard corners. Dennis sighted along the seat; its edge was straight, but the bench rocked on the level concrete. They measured the legs and found one longer than the others. The apprentice marked the excess on its foot before reaching for the plane.
snippets: Pride swelled in Dennis

review.finding: Pride swelled in Dennis is labeled emotion-telling while representing a feeling as material. Resolve the same direct-assertion versus separate-material-construction boundary as the June passage.

remainingErrors.text: Jubilant, Esther carried her citizenship certificate into the cafe. Her gaze floated from the ceiling lights to the tables. The day tasted of warm pastry and possibility rather than ink and anxious silence. Her husband had saved a corner booth, and their son had drawn a flag on every napkin.
snippets: Jubilant

review.finding: Jubilant is an interchangeable narrated feeling label alongside the citizenship celebration.

remainingErrors.text: Eva gave me the larger piece of apple because I had missed dinner. We still had twenty minutes before the last bus. She folded her knife, looked round the shelter, and said, "Feels oddly empty here tonight, somehow. Save that bag for the core."

review.finding: Feels oddly empty here tonight, somehow supplies no described contrast beyond looking around the bus shelter. A literal occupancy observation is possible, but the label needs a documented account of that function. Ordinary dialogue alone supplies no exemption.

remainingErrors.text: The tutor read the student's phrase, "The room became inwardly cold," and asked whether inwardly was the intended word. The recording was muffled at that point. We replayed the sentence twice and heard unbearably instead. She corrected the transcript, leaving the original reading in a note so the typist could check it.

review.finding: The cold-room wording is being checked and corrected against the muffled recording.

remainingErrors.text: The incident report said, "The atmosphere became hostile." I asked Leon what he meant by that. He described a customer pushing the card reader across the counter and blocking the exit from the serving area. We added those actions beneath his original sentence. He wanted to keep the sentence too; he said it was the phrase he'd used when he called the supervisor.

review.finding: The hostile-atmosphere wording is recorded and expanded with the threatening conduct it denotes.

remainingErrors.text: The lunchroom became awkward after Phil asked who had reported his broken van; three colleagues suddenly began clearing their trays. I stayed by the door to prevent him cornering the apprentice. The tension hung heavy in the air. Our manager arrived carrying the inspection report and asked Phil to sit.
snippets: The tension hung heavy in the air.

review.finding: Tension hanging heavy is an independent generic payoff after the observable tray-clearing response.

remainingErrors.text: A different sort of mood inhabited the upstairs landing. My sister taped a folded blanket along the mirror's top edge, then let it unroll over the glass. Our faces disappeared first, then our knees; a narrow strip at the bottom still reflected our shoes. She backed down the steps while I held the upper end of the frame.
snippets: A different sort of mood inhabited the upstairs landing.

review.finding: A different sort of mood is announced without explaining the mood through covering the mirror.

remainingErrors.text: The breakfast counter felt oddly solemn that morning. I turned my cup's chipped rim away from my mouth. Testing her new dental plate, the waitress whistled on the S in "sausages" and abandoned her usual suggestion of extra sauce.
snippets: The breakfast counter felt oddly solemn that morning.

review.finding: The waitress abandoning her usual sauce suggestion can supply the subdued contrast announced by solemn; the denture-related whistling also permits reading the mood as a separate gloss.

remainingErrors.text: The pub became tense when the captain accused the scorer of changing last week's darts results; both teams began checking the chalk marks. I shifted and looked around. Rob turned toward me. The tension was thick enough to cut with a knife. The scorer fetched last week's photograph from his phone to compare the totals.
snippets: The tension was thick enough to cut with a knife.

review.finding: Tension thick enough to cut is independent stock atmosphere beyond the specific darts dispute.

remainingErrors.text: The ferry attendant checked our bicycle tickets and directed us onto the vehicle deck. We moved along together for several paces. A sailor tied the bikes against a rail using rope thicker than my thumb. By the time we reached the passenger cabin, someone had occupied every seat near a socket.
snippets: We moved along together for several paces.

review.finding: Moving together after being directed onto the vehicle deck can provide route continuity to where the bikes are tied; several paces can also be a redundant keeping-pace tag.

remainingErrors.text:
"You could stay here," Dad said, moving the spare key toward me.
I left it on the table. He had already put clean sheets on my old bed; I could see the pillowcase through the open door. Neither of us spoke for a while. Then he drew the key back and asked what time the last bus left.

review.finding: The prolonged nonresponse refuses the offer, and Dad withdraws the key. This was also a historically exposed no-hit demonstration.

remainingErrors.text: The pigeon bobbed its tail with every breath, its beak open despite the cool morning. It let us approach without moving from the pavement. Helena called the rescue number printed on the park notice while I stood between the bird and the feet of people coming out of the station.

review.finding: Tail bobbing with every breath, an open beak in cool weather and immobility describe the condition that leads to a rescue call.

remainingErrors.text: Customer services had my trolley when I came back from the car park. The announcement had given my registration, but the dog was in the silver car beside mine. I explained the mistake to the assistant. She paused for a few seconds before handing me the trolley, and I went back to finish the shopping.
snippets: She paused for a few seconds

review.finding: The assistant pause adds an unexplained interval between accepting the correction and returning the trolley.

remainingErrors.text: The shelter dog's ears twitched at the click of the medicine box, and he disappeared beneath the table. He stayed there when I shook the biscuit tin. I put the tablet inside a piece of cheese and sat on the floor, leaving the box closed behind me.

review.finding: The ear movement at the medicine-box click precedes hiding and explains concealing the box while offering cheese.

remainingErrors.text: The waiting room was silent because the television's sound had been disabled for the hearing tests. My eyes still watered from the wind outside, blurring the boxes on the form. The receptionist brought a large-print copy and a thicker pen. Once I could distinguish the boxes, I paused a little before filling in my address. The pen left a dark line I could follow without leaning over the clipboard.
snippets: I paused a little before filling in my address.

review.finding: Vision has already become adequate when the narrator pauses before entering the address; the pause adds no further role.

remainingErrors.text: The rehearsal room was empty of chairs, which meant we could practice the procession at its full width. Tom's ankle clicked each time he turned, throwing him off the beat. He lingered briefly, then asked to swap places with someone on the outside of the curve.
snippets: He lingered briefly, then asked to swap places with someone on the outside of the curve.

review.finding: Lingering while an ankle throws a dancer off the beat can serve an active physical need before requesting an outside position. The text also permits an unexplained interval after the symptom.

remainingErrors.text: The meeting room felt cold and hollow. May raised one eyebrow at me, the signal we'd agreed on if I started discussing the confidential figures. I changed the subject to delivery dates. She let a moment pass before opening the schedule, then showed the client the revised collection window.
snippets: She let a moment pass before opening the schedule

review.finding: Letting a moment pass may facilitate the confidential-to-delivery topic change; the label treats it as a separate generic pause.

remainingErrors.text: My mouth had gone dry after an hour explaining the route, and the guidebook's place names became difficult to pronounce. Quiet hung around the coach. I lingered briefly before taking a drink. A passenger offered to read out the final villages while I rested my voice, and I passed him the guidebook with my finger under the next stop.
snippets: I lingered briefly before taking a drink.

review.finding: A pause while the mouth is dry and speaking is difficult can rest the voice before drinking; its particular duration and purpose remain implicit.

remainingErrors.text: Grandad raised his eyebrows at the waiter, who brought the bill without interrupting the toast. The room was quiet enough for the guest of honor to speak without a microphone. I let a little time go by before collecting the envelopes, then checked each name against our contributions list.

review.finding: The toast supplies an active reason to delay collecting envelopes until the speaker can finish.

remainingErrors.text: The room felt cold and vacant. Leo's eyes watered when the dust sheet came off the sofa, and he stepped outside to rinse them. He stood there for a little while, then fetched the vacuum. We found enough loose change beneath the cushions to pay for parking.

review.finding: Remaining outside follows rinsing dust-irritated eyes before returning to vacuum the sofa.

remainingErrors.text: The lane was quiet during the factory shutdown, and we could hear the blacksmith's hammer from two streets away. I paused for several seconds before taking the shortcut. My knee had swollen during the walk, so I chose the alley without steps rather than the shorter route beside the church.

review.finding: The pause occurs while choosing the step-free route for a swollen knee.

remainingErrors.text: The librarian found the book in a box awaiting repair. Its cover was detached, but all the pages my mother remembered were still there. Recognition warmed the space between us. We sat at a low table while she showed me the picture that had frightened her when she was seven.
snippets: Recognition warmed the space between us.

review.finding: Recognition warming the space is an ambient reaction tag beyond the specific remembered picture.

remainingErrors.text: There was one empty place at the anniversary dinner, although nobody had cancelled. My sister said she had laid an extra setting out of habit. Loss sat down among us. We moved the spare chair into the hall so the waiter could reach the end of the table.
snippets: Loss sat down among us.

review.finding: Loss taking the spare place may be a generic emotional presence, or an intelligible relation between an absent person and the habitual extra setting.

remainingErrors.text: The shopkeeper said the machine was under warranty, but the serial number had faded off the label. I showed him a photograph taken when I unpacked it. Doubt thickened behind the counter. He enlarged the image on my phone until the last two digits became readable.
snippets: Doubt thickened behind the counter.

review.finding: Doubt thickening adds ambient emotional scenery beyond checking the serial-number photo.

remainingErrors.text: We put the kitten names into a mug. Four slips said Pickle. All four were in my youngest's handwriting. She demanded a recount. The kitten slept across the newspaper while I unfolded the remaining votes, and amusement rippled through the kitchen.
snippets: amusement rippled through the kitchen

review.finding: Amusement rippling can report a family response to the duplicated votes; the formulation also leaves its manifestation generic.

remainingErrors.text: By the time my uncle recognized the tune, the bride's youngest cousin had dragged three reluctant dancers from their chairs and was coming for him. He fetched his wife from the buffet instead; under the merriment floating through the marquee, I could still hear her asking him to put down his plate before he tried to turn her.

review.finding: The dancing, resistance, plate and audible request give the merriment a particular social manifestation.

remainingErrors.text: The room was gloomy and uninviting, with furniture that seemed chosen solely to discourage sitting. I balanced on the edge of a rigid chair while the receptionist checked my appointment.
